title: App shell: tray icon, close to tray, hotkey pause, Windows light/dark and high contrast
friendly: The Snipdeck app: tray icon, closing, light and dark mode
setup: This runs the real Snipdeck app (cargo build --release at the repo root, then target\release\snipdeck-app.exe) on an empty library in spikes-results\m3-data, so your own data is never touched. The first build takes several minutes.
Nothing in this section has ever run on Windows. A failed step is expected to find a bug: write what you saw in the note (n).
Windows 11 hides new tray icons in the overflow flyout (the ^ arrow). Drag the Snipdeck icon out onto the taskbar once so you can see it, or leave it in the flyout and open the flyout for each step.
Have Notepad open with some text typed into it: several steps check that the Panel never takes the keyboard focus from it.
The Panel's close button is the small X in its header. ? then l shows what the app printed (lines starting 'snipdeck:' are warnings such as a missing tray icon or a hotkey that is taken).

tests.title: Start-up: Panel and tray icon appear
tests.do: Wait for the Panel to appear, then find the Snipdeck icon in the notification area (look in the ^ flyout too). Hover over it for a second. Press ? then l to read the app log.
tests.expect: The Panel is on screen and the tray icon is visible; the tooltip reads 'Snipdeck'. The icon is the generic application icon for now (the exe has no icon resource yet): that is not a failure. The log has NO 'snipdeck: tray icon unavailable' and NO 'cannot show the tray icon' line. Hotkey lines are fine.

tests.title: Left click toggles the Panel without taking focus
tests.do: Click into Notepad and type a letter. Left-click the tray icon once: the Panel should hide. Left-click it again: the Panel shows. Look at the Panel's title area and at Notepad's title bar. Click the icon twice quickly.
tests.expect: One click = one change (hide, then show): never hide-then-show from one click. The Panel does not become the active window (Notepad's title bar stays the 'active' colour while the Panel shows). Clicking the tray icon itself makes the taskbar the foreground window, so typing needs a click back into Notepad first: that is Windows' behaviour, not a failure; the Panel must only never take the focus from Notepad on its own (hotkey Ctrl+Alt+Space instead of a tray click: the next letter still goes into Notepad). Two quick clicks end where they began. The Panel does not appear in Alt+Tab.

tests.title: Right click menu
tests.do: Right-click the tray icon. Look at the menu, then click on the desktop to dismiss it. Open it again and press Esc. Open it a third time and click 'Open Panel'.
tests.expect: Menu items in this order: Open Panel, Open Snipdeck, Pause hotkeys, a separator line, Quit. The menu opens at the icon (above the taskbar, not off screen). Clicking elsewhere closes it at once (it must not stay open), and so does Esc. 'Open Panel' shows the Panel if hidden. The menu is light even in dark mode: that is known, record it only if it looks wrong otherwise. After the menu closes by a click elsewhere or Esc, the app restores the window that was in front when the menu opened (the taskbar after a tray click, so keys may still need a click back into Notepad): record if keys go nowhere at all, for instance a letter typed after dismissing the menu does nothing even after clicking Notepad.

tests.title: Keyboard use of the tray icon
tests.do: Win+B, then arrow keys to the Snipdeck icon (open the ^ flyout with Enter if needed). Press Enter. Press Win+B again, arrow to the icon and press the Menu key (or Shift+F10).
tests.expect: Enter on the icon toggles the Panel (same as a left click). Menu key / Shift+F10 opens the same menu. Enter or Esc closes it.

tests.title: Pause hotkeys
tests.do: With the Panel shown, press Ctrl+Alt+Space (it should hide the Panel; press it again to show). Right-click the tray icon and choose 'Pause hotkeys'. Press Ctrl+Alt+Space. Open the menu again and look at 'Pause hotkeys'. Choose it again. Press Ctrl+Alt+Space.
tests.expect: While paused: Ctrl+Alt+Space does nothing, and 'Pause hotkeys' shows a check mark in the menu. After choosing it again: the check is gone and Ctrl+Alt+Space toggles the Panel again. The tray left click works the whole time. The log shows no 'cannot register' line after resuming (if it does, another app took the chord while paused: record it).

tests.title: Close to tray
tests.do: Click the X in the Panel header. Look at Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc): is snipdeck-app.exe still listed? Left-click the tray icon. (The Esc key on an empty search box is not tested: the Panel is non-activating and takes no keyboard focus yet, see the known gaps in docs/HANDOVER.md.)
tests.expect: The X hides the Panel; the tray icon stays and snipdeck-app.exe keeps running. Left click brings the Panel back. The app does NOT quit. Skip anything about Esc: known gap.

tests.title: Open Snipdeck (stand-in)
tests.do: Hide the Panel, then choose 'Open Snipdeck' from the tray menu.
tests.expect: For now it shows the Panel (the main window does not exist yet, M4). Record if nothing happens.

tests.title: Quit removes the icon at once
tests.do: Choose 'Quit' in the tray menu. Check Task Manager. Move the mouse over the spot where the tray icon was (and the ^ flyout).
tests.expect: The Panel closes and snipdeck-app.exe disappears from Task Manager. The tray icon is gone immediately: no ghost icon that vanishes only when hovered. The wizard may show the app as exited.

tests.title: Explorer restart brings the icon back
tests.do: The wizard relaunched the app. Open a terminal and run: taskkill /f /im explorer.exe  then, if the taskbar does not return by itself, run: start explorer.exe . When the taskbar is back, look for the Snipdeck icon and left-click it twice.
tests.expect: The Snipdeck icon is back in the notification area without restarting Snipdeck (this is the TaskbarCreated message). Left click still toggles the Panel and the right-click menu still works. If the icon does NOT return, record it: that is the bug this step exists to find. While Explorer is gone the Panel's X must not strand the app: if you press the Panel's X in that window the app quits (no icon to return from) rather than hiding invisibly.

tests.title: Icon at other display scales
tests.do: Settings > System > Display > Scale: set 150%, look at the tray icon, then 200%, then back to 100% (sign out is not needed on Windows 11).
tests.expect: The icon stays sharp enough to recognise at each scale and the tooltip still shows; the right-click menu text is sharp, not blurry or stretched, at 150% and 200%. (It is the generic application icon until the exe gets its own.)

tests.title: Windows dark mode is followed live
tests.do: Make sure no settings file forces a theme (the default is 'system'). Open Settings > Personalization > Colors > Choose your mode. Pick Dark, look at the Panel; pick Light, look again. Leave the Panel visible while you do it.
tests.expect: The Panel turns dark within about a second of choosing Dark, and light again for Light, WITHOUT restarting Snipdeck and without clicking the Panel. Record how long it takes. The Panel's text stays readable in both.

tests.title: Theme setting overrides Windows
tests.do: Quit Snipdeck from the tray. Create spikes-results\m3-data\settings.json containing {"theme": "dark"} (Notepad is fine). Set Windows to Light mode and relaunch with ? then r. Then change the file to {"theme": "light"}, set Windows to Dark, relaunch with ? then r.
tests.expect: With theme=dark the Panel is dark although Windows is Light, and with theme=light the Panel is light although Windows is Dark; changing the Windows mode while it runs changes nothing. Afterwards restore your Windows mode.

tests.title: High contrast
tests.do: Press Left Alt + Left Shift + Print Screen and confirm (this turns on the default High Contrast theme). Look at the Panel while Snipdeck is running. Press the same keys again to turn it off.
tests.expect: The Panel switches to the system high-contrast colours (window background, text, highlight) while it is on, and returns to normal when you turn it off, without restarting Snipdeck. Record what looks wrong: much of the Panel may still be drawn in its normal palette, because the UI components only partly read the high-contrast colours so far.

tests.title: A damaged settings file is set aside, not lost
tests.do: Quit Snipdeck from the tray. Overwrite spikes-results\m3-data\settings.json with the text: { "panel_width": 400, "no_paste_apps": ["keepass.exe"  (cut off, no closing brackets). Relaunch with ? then r. Then look in spikes-results\m3-data.
tests.expect: Snipdeck starts normally using what could be salvaged from the file (only the no-paste list can be recovered from cut-off text, so keepass.exe is still excluded from auto-paste and everything else is at its default; no crash, no error dialog). The folder now has settings.json.bad with exactly the damaged text, and a NEW valid settings.json written at launch that holds those salvaged values. Quit and relaunch: keepass.exe is still excluded from auto-paste and no new .bad appears. A file with valid JSON but a wrong value type, such as {"theme": 7}, is also moved to .bad; {"panel_width": 9999} is not (it is just clamped). Also: a settings.json saved by Notepad as 'UTF-8 with BOM' (or 'Unicode', UTF-16) is read normally and is NOT moved to .bad.

tests.title: Settings are written (needs a Settings window)
tests.do: Not testable yet: no screen in the app changes a setting, so nothing writes settings.json in a real run. Skip this step. When the Settings window exists (M4) check: change a setting, find settings.json updated about half a second later, kill the process from Task Manager right after a change and confirm settings.json is either the old or the new file, never half-written; no settings.json.tmp is left behind.
tests.expect: Skip. The writing logic (atomic temp-and-rename, debounce) is covered by tests on Linux with a fixed clock; the Windows rename-over-existing behaviour has not been run.

tests.title: A close request from outside quits the app, tray included
tests.do: With Snipdeck running (launch with ? then r if needed), open a terminal and run: taskkill /im snipdeck-app.exe  (no /f). Check Task Manager and the notification area.
tests.expect: The app exits within a second and the tray icon disappears with it. It must NOT keep running without a tray icon (that would be the hidden window being closed by the request).

tests.title: Elevated: the icon returns after an Explorer restart
tests.do: Run the wizard (right-click Test Snipdeck on Windows.bat, then Run as administrator) so Snipdeck is elevated, launch step 9 again and restart Explorer as there.
tests.expect: The icon comes back although Snipdeck is elevated (TaskbarCreated is let through the integrity filter). If it does not, record it.

tests.title: Demo: every Panel control answers a click (with the diagnostic log on)
tests.do: Quit any Snipdeck still running (tray menu Quit, or Task Manager). The wizard starts the demo with SNIPDECK_LOG=1. Click, in this order, waiting a second after each: (1) the board name 'Work' top left, (2) 'Personal' in the menu that opens, (3) the board name again and 'Work', (4) the 'Addresses' tab, (5) the 'Email replies' tab, (6) the first pinned chip, (7) the first row, (8) the + after the tabs, (9) the pin button, (10) the X. Then press 'l'.
tests.expect: (1) a menu listing Work and Personal opens under the board name; (2) the Panel shows the Personal board (an Errands tab); (3) back on Work; (4)/(5) the rows change with the tab; (6)/(7) a toast says the item was pasted or copied; (8) a new 'New list' tab appears and is selected; (9) the pin button toggles its filled look; (10) the Panel hides to the tray. In the log (? then l) every click shows a 'snipdeck-log ... pointer Pressed Left at physical (x, y) = logical (x, y), scale s' line followed by a 'snipdeck-log ... callback on_<name>' line (on_board_menu_requested, on_board_menu_activated (1), on_tab_selected (1), on_pinned_used (0), on_row_activated (0), on_add_list_requested, on_pin_toggled (false), on_close_requested and 'effect HidePanel'). Note the number of every click that did nothing, and copy the log lines around it into the note: a pointer line with no callback line means the click missed the control (scale or position), no pointer line at all means the window never got the click.

tests.title: First run on an empty real library is usable
tests.do: Quit Snipdeck. Delete the folder spikes-results\m3-first-run if it exists (the wizard then starts on a brand-new library, as Snipdeck.bat with no command does on a new PC). Copy some text in Notepad. Click the board name, then the board in its menu, then 'Save from clipboard', then the + after the tabs. Press ? then l.
tests.expect: The board switcher reads 'My snippets' (not blank), its menu lists 'My snippets', the copied text appears as a row in the 'Snippets' list with a 'Saved' toast, and + adds a 'New list' tab. The log has 'real library; starter board made: true' on this first launch (false on the next).

tests.title: Windows open fully in view at 100, 150 and 225 % scaling
tests.do: Open the Panel, then the Main window (tray menu: Open Snipdeck) and Settings. In Windows Settings > System > Display > Scale choose 100%, then 150%, then 225% (225% needs Custom scaling and signing out and in once; the wizard continues where you left off afterwards). At each scale open the Panel, the Main window, Settings and one right-click menu and look at each. Put the scale back to your normal value at the end.
tests.expect: At every scale each window opens fully on screen near where you opened it, never partly off an edge. Settings fits the visible screen at 150% and 225% with its buttons reachable (it scrolls inside if needed). Text and icons are sharp and not cut off, and a menu is as wide as its longest item. Nothing has run on Windows yet: write what you saw in the note (? then n).

tests.title: The Windows file dialog opens in front and works (Import)
tests.do: In Settings find Your data and press Import. Choose a source that asks for a file or a folder (for example a folder with a few .txt files). When the Windows file dialog opens, press Cancel once. Open it again and pick the folder or file.
tests.expect: The Windows file dialog opens in front of Snipdeck, not hidden behind it, and the Panel does not appear on top of it. Cancel returns to Snipdeck with nothing changed. Picking a file or folder shows a preview of what would be added. Snipdeck stays responsive throughout.

tests.title: Panel dock to a screen edge: fold and hover
tests.do: In Settings > Panel dock set Dock to = Right edge and Open a docked panel by = Hover. Move the pointer away and wait about half a second, then rest the pointer on the thin strip at the screen edge. Then try Click and Hover and click, and finally set Dock to back to Floating.
tests.expect: The Panel sits against the right edge of the monitor it is on. With Hover it folds into a thin strip after the Leave delay (about 0.4 s) and unfolds when the pointer rests on the strip for the Hover delay (about 0.15 s), without taking keyboard focus from Notepad. With Click it opens only on a click. Floating gives the free Panel back.

tests.title: Dock from the lower middle of the screen
tests.do: Set Dock to = Floating. Drag the Panel so it sits in the lower middle of the screen, just above the taskbar and a little left of centre. Open the Panel's three-dots menu and read its dock row, then choose it. Choose the row again to undock.
tests.expect: The row reads Dock to the left edge (Dock to the right edge when the Panel is right of centre), never the bottom edge where the taskbar is. Choosing it moves the Panel once to that edge, full height, with no flicker and no snap back to floating. The second choice (Undock the panel) gives the floating Panel back where it was.

tests.title: Drag the Panel to a screen edge to dock it
tests.do: With the Panel floating, drag it by its header until its right side is within about 16 px of the right edge of the screen, hold still for a moment, then release. Then drag it down until its bottom is next to the taskbar and release there. Finally, in Settings > Panel dock, pick Bottom edge.
tests.expect: Near the right edge a thin accent strip shows along the Panel's right side; about a quarter of a second after you stop moving, the Panel docks to the right edge. Next to the taskbar no strip shows and the Panel stays floating where you dropped it. Picking Bottom edge in Settings shows the message The taskbar is on that edge and the Panel stays floating.

tests.title: Stray marks in text: send a crop
tests.do: Open the main window on All items and look at a list chip such as Snippets, then open an empty list to see This list is empty. If you see a stray dot or mark over or next to any letter, press Win+Shift+S, draw a tight box around the mark and the word, and paste the crop into your report together with the window name and your display scale (Settings > System > Display > Scale, for example 125%).
tests.expect: Normally there is no mark. The developers cannot reproduce one at 100% or 225% scale on their machine, so the crop plus the scale is what lets them find the cause.

tests.title: No see-through window after Alt+Tab or restore (O39)
tests.do: Open the Main window and the Panel next to a busy window (for example Notepad with text). Press Alt+Tab to switch away from Main and back to it 20 times, then do the same with the Panel 20 times. Then minimise Main and restore it from the taskbar 5 times. Look at the whole window each time, not only the title bar.
tests.expect: At no point is any part of the Main window or the Panel see-through: the client area always shows the Snipdeck background and content, never the windows behind it, and never only the border and title bar. Write the step and the count in the note (n) if you ever saw it.

tests.title: First paste after a cold start is the right item
tests.do: Close Snipdeck completely (tray icon, Quit), then start it again. Before doing anything else, copy the word OLDCLIP in Notepad (so it is the newest thing on your clipboard and at the top of Win+V). Click into an empty Notepad, then open the Snipdeck Panel and, as the very first action, click an item whose text is not OLDCLIP. Do this once right after start and once more after hiding and showing the Panel.
tests.expect: The item you clicked is pasted both times, never OLDCLIP. If the clipboard cannot take the item in time, nothing is pasted and a toast says the clipboard was busy; pressing the item again works. Report any case where OLDCLIP (or any other earlier clipboard text) is pasted instead.

tests.title: Delete on a list or board shows only the confirmation (O52)
tests.do: In the Panel right-click a list tab and choose 'Delete list...'. Wait 3 seconds, then press Cancel. Do it again with the tab's Menu key (or Shift+F10) and press Esc. Then in the Main window open the board menu (click the board name) and choose 'Delete board...', wait 3 seconds and press Cancel.
tests.expect: Each time only the delete confirmation appears, inside the Panel or the Main window. No list editor or board editor window opens, before or after it, and nothing flashes behind it. Cancel and Esc close it and the list or board is still there. With only one board, 'Delete board...' is greyed out.

tests.title: No white flash when a window opens (O52)
tests.do: Set Settings > Theme to Dark. Open each of these three times, closing it between: the list editor (Panel: right-click a tab, 'Edit list...'), the item editor (double-click a row), Settings, Troubleshoot (Panel kebab menu), the board editor (Main: board menu, 'Rename board...'), and the Move chooser (Main: right-click a row, Move to...). Watch each window as it appears. Then set Theme to Light and open the list editor and Settings again.
tests.expect: Every window appears in the theme's background colour from its first visible moment: no white or blank frame, not even for a split second, on the first open or on later ones. In Light the first colour is the light background, not pure white. Write any window that flashed in the note (n).

tests.title: Windows open beside the window they came from (O41)
tests.do: Put the Panel on the left of the screen with free space to its right. Open Settings from the Panel menu, close it, then open Troubleshoot and the item editor (New snippet). Then drag the Panel to the far right edge of the screen and open Settings again. Then drag the Panel to the middle of a small or 150 percent scaled screen so there is no room on either side, and open Settings once more. Finally open Settings from the Main window while the Main window is maximised.
tests.expect: With room to its right, each window opens just right of the Panel with a small even gap (about 8 px at 100 percent, scaled on other displays), lined up with the Panel's top, fully on the screen and clear of the taskbar. At the right edge it opens on the left of the Panel instead. With no room at the sides it opens below or above the Panel, or covers as little of it as it can. Over a maximised Main window it opens centred. It never opens half off screen or under the taskbar.

tests.title: Take screenshot from the Panel, the tray and the palette (O48)
tests.do: Open Paint. Open the Panel menu and choose Take screenshot. Drag a rectangle over part of the screen with the snipping overlay, then paste into Paint with Ctrl+V. Repeat from the tray icon menu (Take screenshot) and from the command palette (type screenshot). Then turn on Settings > Keep Panel visible during screenshots and repeat once. Then start a screenshot, press Esc on the overlay without taking one, and wait a minute.
tests.expect: On choosing Take screenshot the Panel disappears at once, so it is not in front of the snipping overlay, and the overlay appears. When the snip is taken the clipboard holds the picture and the Panel is shown again within about half a second, without taking focus from the app in front. With the setting on, the Panel stays on screen during the snip. After Esc the Panel returns on its own after about 60 seconds. If the overlay cannot start, the Panel is shown at once with a toast saying so. No snippet is added by itself.

tests.title: Closing Main closes what it opened (O53)
tests.do: Open the Main window. From it open Settings, the Troubleshoot window, the Tag manager and an item editor (type a few new words in the item's text, do not save), then a list editor (change its name, do not save). Also open the command palette (Ctrl+K). Close the Main window with its X button. Then open Main again from the tray, open the same item and the same list for editing. Next open the Panel, open Settings and an item editor from the Panel, and close Main: they must stay. Then close the Panel with its X button.
tests.expect: Closing Main closes Settings, Troubleshoot, the Tag manager, both editors and the palette together with it, with no question asked. Main opens again with no palette. The item editor and the list editor come back with the words you typed (the item editor says the draft was restored). Closing Main does not close the windows opened from the Panel. Closing the Panel then closes Settings and the editor opened from it. Write which window stayed open, if any, in the note (n).

tests.title: The Panel footer is fully visible at the regular size (O45)
tests.do: Open the Panel at its normal size (do not resize it). Look at the bottom strip. Then set Windows display scale to 125% and 150% (Settings > System > Display), sign out and in if asked, and open the Panel again each time.
tests.expect: The bottom strip (\

tests.title: Reset size and position (O45)
tests.do: Drag the Panel to the other side of the screen and resize it very small. Open the Panel menu (the three dots) and choose 'Reset size and position'. Then press Ctrl+K in the Main window, type 'reset' and run 'Reset Panel size and position'. If you have two monitors, move the Panel to the second one first and check the first one's saved place is untouched.
tests.expect: The Panel jumps back to its default size and place at once, with no Undo message. It stays there after you close and reopen it. On a second monitor only that monitor's place is forgotten.

tests.title: Add an item with the New item row (O45)
tests.do: In the Panel click '+ New item' under the last item (also try it in an empty list). Paste some text and press Enter. Then press Ctrl+N, paste a web address and click Create. Try Shift+Enter (new line) and Esc (cancel). Click the Sensitive switch before creating once.
tests.expect: The row is easy to see. The box opens with the cursor in it and the kind already set (Link for a web address). Enter or Create adds the item under the last one, selects it and clears the box. Shift+Enter makes a new line. Esc closes the box and keeps nothing. A Sensitive item shows hidden.

tests.title: Select several items and act on them (O45)
tests.do: In the Panel Ctrl+click two rows, Shift+click a third, then press Ctrl+A and Shift+Down. Use the bar that appears: Move to..., Colour, Copy all, Delete. Paste after Copy all. Press Esc to clear. Hover a row and look for the three dots on it, and look at the selected row.
tests.expect: The bar says how many are selected. Move to and Colour ask once and change all of them. Copy all pastes the texts one after another. Delete removes them with an Undo message and no question. Esc clears the selection. The three dots show on the hovered and the selected row and open the row menu.

tests.title: Show numbers (O45)
tests.do: Open the Panel menu (three dots) and switch 'Show numbers' off, then on. With it off press Alt+1 and 1 on a row.
tests.expect: With it off the row numbers are gone and the 1-9 keys still use rows. With it on they come back. The choice is kept after restarting.

tests.title: Undo and redo (O47)
tests.do: Open the Panel. Delete an item (it shows an Undo message), then press Ctrl+Z and then Ctrl+Y. Pin an item, move one to another list, then press Ctrl+Z twice and Ctrl+Y once. Use the Undo and Redo buttons in the Panel header and in the Main toolbar. Hover the buttons. Delete a list in Main and press the Undo button on the message.
tests.expect: Ctrl+Z takes back the last change and says what it undid; Ctrl+Y brings it back. The Undo message button does the same for its own change. The header and toolbar buttons are greyed when there is nothing to undo or redo, and their tooltips name the change they would undo or redo. Write which change was not undone correctly in the note (n).
